name: OpptiAI Website Auditor
author: Benjamin Graham Oats

sections.description:
OpptiAI Website Auditor is a free WordPress plugin that checks your site and shows what needs fixing. The scan runs inside WordPress, needs no account, and sends nothing to OpptiAI unless you turn on usage stats. Results in under a minute.

It checks:

  • Images in your media library that have no alt text, and images in your pages and posts whose file is larger than 300 KB.
  • SEO titles that are missing, used on more than one page, shorter than 20 or longer than 65 characters, and meta descriptions that are missing, shorter than 70 or longer than 165 characters.
  • Posts with very little text: under 300 words, or under 600 characters in languages written without spaces, such as Chinese, Japanese and Thai.
  • Pages and posts with no internal links pointing to them. This check uses the scan from OpptiAI Internal Linking 0.1.4 or later, so it runs only when that plugin is active. OpptiAI Internal Linking suggests links and applies them only when you click Apply.
  • Whether robots.txt, an XML sitemap and llms.txt can be found, whether your site address is set to HTTPS, and whether search engines are allowed to index the site.

Page checks read your newest 500 published posts and pages, and the results say how many were checked, for example “Checked 500 of 650 published pages and posts.” Alt text is checked across your whole media library. When OpptiAI Titles has already scanned your site, missing and duplicate title counts come from that scan.

Your score uses only what the scan measured. Areas this version doesn’t measure (structured data, page speed and accessibility), and files WordPress couldn’t fetch from your own site, are shown as “Not checked” and don’t count toward your score. Pages with no internal links are reported but don’t change your score.

Image findings link to OpptiAI Alt Text, and title and description findings link to OpptiAI Titles. The Auditor never changes your site. Fixes happen in Alt Text or Titles.

Optional usage stats: an administrator can turn on “Share usage stats” on the plugin’s first-run screen (before the first scan) or on its Account screen. It is off by default, and nothing is sent unless it is turned on. See External services for what is sent.

External services

By default this plugin doesn’t connect to any external service. Every scan runs inside WordPress and nothing is sent to OpptiAI. To check robots.txt, the sitemap and llms.txt, WordPress requests those files from your own site. A sitemap address listed in robots.txt is only requested when it is on your own site. Usage stats (PostHog, below) are also off unless an administrator turns them on.

The plugin also contains an optional full scan that uses the OpptiAI API. It is switched off. It can only be switched on by adding define( 'OPPTI_OPT_ENABLE_CLOUD_SCAN', true ); to wp-config.php, and even then nothing is sent until an administrator chooses “Allow full scan” in the plugin.

Service: OpptiAI API
Service URL: https://alttext-ai-backend.onrender.com
Website: https://oppti.dev
Purpose: Run a full scan from the OpptiAI server, show scan history and progress, connect an OpptiAI account, show credit usage and open billing.
When data is sent: Only when the setting above is added and an administrator has chosen “Allow full scan”. Then data is sent when a full scan runs, when scan history, progress or credit usage loads, when an administrator signs in or creates an account, and when an administrator opens billing.
Data sent: Your site’s URL and a pseudonymous ID created for this install (or reused from another OpptiAI plugin), with every request. During a full scan the OpptiAI server then visits your site’s public pages. Signing in or creating an account sends the email address and password entered, and the returned account token is stored in your WordPress database. Loading credit usage and opening billing also send your account token or license key, including one stored by OpptiAI Alt Text on this site.
Privacy Policy: https://oppti.dev/privacy
Terms of Use: https://oppti.dev/terms

Service: PostHog (usage stats, opt-in only)
Service URL: https://us.i.posthog.com
Website: https://posthog.com
Purpose: Understand which features are used so OpptiAI can improve the plugin.
When data is sent: Only after an administrator turns on “Share usage stats” on the plugin’s first-run screen or Account screen. It is off by default, nothing is sent or queued before you opt in, and turning it off stops sending immediately. While it is on, an event is sent when a plugin screen is opened, when a scan starts, finishes or fails, when a Fix, Install, How to fix or Upgrade button is clicked, when the setting is turned on, once per site when you first opt in (to record that the plugin is active), and when the plugin is deactivated.
Data sent: The event name; scan results as numbers only (the score, how many pages, posts and images were checked, how many checks found something or weren’t checked, and how long the scan took); which OpptiAI plugin and which check a Fix or Install button was for, and the screen it was on; which check a How to fix button was for, that it was a How to fix click, and the screen it was on; for an Upgrade Plan button or the signed-out “Get more from OpptiAI” link, the screen it was on, which check it came from (if any), which of those buttons it was and, for the signed-out link, that it was the guest link; which other OpptiAI plugins are active; the plugin, WordPress and PHP versions; whether the site is a test or staging site; and a random ID created for this install when you opt in. It never sends your site address or domain, page content, titles, URLs, post or image IDs, emails, usernames, license keys or IP addresses.
Privacy Policy: https://posthog.com/privacy
Terms of Use: https://posthog.com/terms

Source code

The admin app ships with its human-readable source: the JavaScript and JSX files in prototype/, build.js and package.json. prototype/dist/app.bundle.js is built from them. To rebuild it, run npm install and then npm run build in the plugin folder. The bundle includes React and ReactDOM (MIT license).
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin and activate it.
  2. Open “OpptiAI Website Auditor” in the admin menu.
  3. Click “Run free audit”.
sections.faq:
Does the scan change my site?

No. The scan only reads. Fixes happen in the linked OpptiAI plugin, when you choose to make them.

Does it work on a local or private site?

Yes. The scan runs inside WordPress, so it works on local and private sites too.

Why does a check say “Not checked”?

Either this version doesn’t measure that area, or WordPress couldn’t load a file such as robots.txt from your own site. Some hosts block those requests. Tools, then Site Health, shows whether they work. A check that says “Not checked” isn’t a problem and doesn’t count toward your score.

Why are pages with no internal links “Not checked”?

That check uses the scan from OpptiAI Internal Linking 0.1.4 or later. Activate it, then run the audit again.

Do I need an account?

No. Audits run inside WordPress and need no account.

Does the plugin collect any data?

Not unless you choose to. “Share usage stats” on the Account screen is off by default. If you turn it on, the plugin sends anonymous feature usage to PostHog, as described under External services, and you can turn it off again at any time. Deleting the plugin removes the setting and its random install ID.

Where can I get help?

Post in the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org, or email support@oppti.dev.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Each finding now links straight to where you can fix it.
  • Pages that were not checked no longer show an empty “Not checked” state. You see a reason, or a Run check button.
  • Fixed: if you opt in to usage analytics, the plugin can now record that it was activated.

1.0.2

  • Install buttons now open the right plugin’s own page instead of a search.
  • Step-by-step fixes for missing alt text, missing SEO titles, duplicate titles and long titles.
  • “See how to fix” now opens the steps for manual fixes such as llms.txt.
  • After you activate the plugin, the Auditor dashboard opens. The Plugins screen also has Get started and Settings links.
  • You can choose whether to share usage stats before your first scan. It stays off unless you say yes.
  • Upgrade and install links now note which check they came from.
  • More reliable when other OpptiAI plugins are active.
  • Usage stats records when sharing is switched on.
  • Re-run Audit now starts a new scan.
  • Shows a loading message while the Auditor opens.

1.0.1

  • Admin styles and scripts now load as separate files on the plugin screen only.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Optional usage stats: an administrator can turn on “Share usage stats” on the Account screen. It is off by default, and nothing is sent without it.
